title: Uniform Ext bound
statement:
Let $\Lambda=E$ or $\Qlb$. For every $C\in\Cons(X,\Lambda)$ there is an integer $d_C\geq0$ such that

$$
\Ext^q_{\Lambda}(C,N)=0
\qquad\text{for all }q>d_C\text{ and all }N\in\Cons(X,\Lambda),
$$

the Ext groups being taken in $\D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$.

For $C=a_!L$, with $a$ factored as $S\hookrightarrow Z\hookrightarrow X$ and $j$ the open complement of
$Z$, the proof gives $d_C=\operatorname{cd}_\ell(j)+\operatorname{cd}_\ell(S)+2$ (cohomological
dimensions as in [sk-def-cd]). One of the two extra degrees comes from the cone defining
$R\underline\Gamma_Z$, the other from a derived inverse limit over the reductions modulo $\pi_E^n$.

proof.text: Partial Lean proof, existence clause: the base is finite or algebraically closed up to field isomorphism. The base-field cohomological-dimension theorem and the finite-type absolute and relative bounds make every refined source cutoff finite. A finite supremum of these cutoffs is finite, including the empty supremum zero. The separate theorem uniformConstructibleExt_cutoff also proves finiteness of the original displayed open-closed expression, without claiming vanishing at that expression.

proof.text: Fix a degree above that cutoff. The coefficient-heart filtration writes each target as finite extensions of locally closed lisse pieces. Covariant Ext exactness and zero-object vanishing prove the same bound for every constructible target. Then fix the source filtration, take the finite maximum of its natural bounds, and use contravariant Ext exactness to prove uniformConstructibleExt_exists. Isomorphisms of quotients are handled by composition with degree-zero Ext classes; bottom and top subobjects are transported by their canonical isomorphisms.
